question: How do the 16 twisted Pati-Salam, 27 chiral E6, 32 ordinary-real Spin(10)/Pati-Salam, and 54 ordinary-real E6 routes compare when state-count conventions and real structures are kept explicit?

sources.use: E6 matter 27, scalar 27/351-prime/650 content, and renormalizable Yukawa-sector precedent
the E6 cubic 27_F 27_F 27_H and singlet-VEV masses for vectorlike 10-sector exotics
Spin(10) 10/120/126 Yukawa channels and scalar-completion context

countingConvention.unit: complex internal one-particle dimensions in an all-left-handed convention
countingConvention.chiralMatterCount: counts independent left-handed fermion components before adding an ordinary charge-conjugate carrier
countingConvention.realCarrierCount: counts a representation and its conjugate as separate complex summands on which an antiunitary J exchanges them
countingConvention.warning: A real-carrier count is not automatically a count of independent propagating left-handed fields. If the second summand is the J-related antiparticle copy, calling it a mirror family is a category error; if both summands are independent fields, the theory is vectorlike and mirror decoupling becomes a dynamical problem.

brokenPatiSalamTruncationOf27.formula: 16 + bar16 + 10 + 1 after discarding E6 and U(1)_psi covariance
brokenPatiSalamTruncationOf27.boundary: representation-theoretically ordinary-real under the broken Pati-Salam/Spin(10) stage, but not a complete E6 representation and therefore not one of the four ultraviolet routes

patiSalam16.verdict: semisimple perturbative anomaly free and both SU(2) Witten parities even

e6Chiral27.verdict: the standard chiral E6 family is anomaly consistent; the displayed subgroup traces cancel

ordinaryReal32And54.verdict: representation plus conjugate is vectorlike at the gauge-representation level, so local gauge anomalies cancel pairwise

anomalyChecks.boundary: A twisted or disconnected extension still requires its own discrete/global anomaly audit.

routes.J: J g = sigma_LR(g) J, where sigma_LR exchanges SU(2)_L and SU(2)_R
routes.anomalyStatus: continuous Pati-Salam anomaly tests pass; disconnected-extension test open
routes.scalarClosure: not closed: cross-chiral edges require (1,2,2) or (15,2,2), while Majorana and high-scale breaking require additional multiplets
routes.mirrorStatus: no extra conjugate carrier, but ordinary low-energy reality must emerge after the twist is broken
routes.minimality: smallest of the four counts, conditional on admitting the left-right twist
routes.killTest: construct the disconnected/twisted action and show J^2, the fermionic action, discrete anomaly cancellation, symmetry breaking, and recovery of ordinary low-energy charge conjugation

routes.J: no ordinary internal J closes on one complex 27; an E6 outer-automorphism-twisted J is a separate disconnected-extension proposal
routes.twistedJ: possible in representation type, not audited as a full disconnected model
routes.anomalyStatus: chiral E6 matter route is anomaly consistent
routes.scalarClosure: not closed by the fermion 27: the cubic 27_F 27_F 27_H supplies 16_F16_F10_H and 10_F10_F1_H channels, but a conventional 126 Majorana branch requires 351-prime_H and realistic E6 breaking requires further scalar data
routes.mirrorStatus: the Spin(10) 10 is vectorlike after further branching and can receive mass from a singlet VEV, but the whole 10+1 exotic mass matrix and retained chiral index must be shown
routes.minimality: smallest standard simple-parent enlargement containing the family 16 in the E6 fundamental, but not a real carrier
routes.killTest: write the complete 27_F exotic mass matrix after declared 27/351-prime/breaking VEVs and prove that exactly the intended 16-sector chirality remains light while the one-parent-invariant relation survives the vacuum and thresholds

routes.J: ordinary gauge-equivariant antiunitary exchange between 16 and bar16
routes.anomalyStatus: pairwise vectorlike cancellation; each intended one-family Pati-Salam restriction also passes its anomaly test
routes.scalarClosure: not closed by the carrier: Dirac, Majorana and breaking sectors still require declared 10/126 and breaking representations
routes.mirrorStatus: safe only if bar16 is the constrained J-antiparticle copy; if it is an independent left-handed field, 16+bar16 is vectorlike and an invariant mass can remove the desired family together with the mirror
routes.minimality: minimum ordinary-J closure of a fixed Spin(10) 16 or fixed Pati-Salam family
routes.killTest: specify the fermionic-action/reality projection. If both summands are independent, exhibit a symmetry-respecting mass matrix with chiral index one; otherwise identify bar16 explicitly as the non-independent antiparticle carrier

routes.J: ordinary gauge-equivariant antiunitary exchange between 27 and bar27
routes.scalarClosure: not closed by the carrier and inherits the E6 27/351-prime/breaking-field inventory plus its conjugation requirements
routes.mirrorStatus: safe as a kinematic J-pair; if treated as two independent chiral multiplets it is vectorlike and the gauge-invariant 27 bar27 mass does not selectively preserve one 27
routes.minimality: minimum ordinary-J closure of an E6 27, not the minimum E6 chiral matter representation
routes.killTest: separate the J-related antiparticle copy from independent matter, then demonstrate full exotic lifting, scalar vacuum, thresholds and one surviving chiral family without silently breaking the asserted reality law

categoryTheorem.fixedPatiSalamSpectrum: For the fixed sixteen-component Pati-Salam family, the two reality implementations in claim 1559 are exhaustive: 16 with left-right-twisted J or 32 with ordinary J.
categoryTheorem.parentEnlargement: Once parent-spectrum enlargement is admitted, the phrase exactly two honest branches is incomplete: a chiral E6 27 and its 54-dimensional ordinary-real completion are additional routes.
categoryTheorem.nonEquivalence: The 27 is not a third ordinary-real solution between 16 and 32. It changes the matter content by adding a Spin(10) 10+1 and still needs either no internal ordinary J, an outer-automorphism twist, or the 54 completion. A 43-dimensional 16+bar16+10+1 closure exists only after abandoning ultraviolet E6 and U(1)_psi covariance.
correctedBranching: E6-enlarged: 27 chiral (optionally separately test an outer twist) or 54 ordinary-real

comparativeDecision.claim1559MateriallyFalse: unscoped yes; scoped to the fixed Pati-Salam family spectrum no
comparativeDecision.bestEconomicalTest: 16 twisted, because it adds no fermionic exotics but bears the strongest disconnected-reality burden
comparativeDecision.bestSimpleParentTest: 27 chiral E6, because it is anomaly consistent and supplies a parent cubic plus vectorlike 10-sector mass channel, but it bears an exotic/scalar-completion burden
comparativeDecision.bestConservativeRealityTest: 32 ordinary-real Spin(10)/Pati-Salam, provided the conjugate is explicitly a J-related antiparticle carrier rather than an independent mirror field
comparativeDecision.largestControlRoute: 54 ordinary-real E6, useful as a completeness control but dominated in minimality unless ordinary E6-equivariant J is mandatory
comparativeDecision.noWinnerYet: None of the four routes closes the scalar, Ward-intertwiner, threshold and physical-observable gates.
